description.narrative: Gaza’s entire population of 2.2 million people is in urgent need of humanitarian assistance to meet their critical needs, in a context where the situation has already been dire prior to the current escalation in October 2023. According to OCHA (15 April 2024), over 33,797 people are reported killed by the conflict to date, over 70% of whom are women and children, and 76,465 people have been injured . Latest estimates suggest that 1.7 million people have been displaced , on average 3 times since the conflict began and living in crowded shelters with limited access to food, water, and sanitation facilities. Famine is imminent as 1.1 million people, halfthe population of Gaza, experience catastrophic food insecurity, continued to be exacerbated by the limited humanitarian access throughout Gaza, particularly in Northern Gaza . Damage to infrastructure and limited fuel impede water production and have rendered Gaza with only approximately 7% of its pre-escalation water quantities. One out of three water pipelines coming from Israel is only functioning at 72% of its full capacity, with no access to clean water in Northern Gaza . Average household consumption of water is far less than recommended minimum standards. Seven months after the beginning of the war,the entire population of Gaza is enduring severe risk to their lives. Specifically, women and children are impacted more disproportionately by the current conflict . With water scarcity looming and demanding immediate action. Oxfam is committed to providing safe water for drinking and cooking purposes to approximately 5,150 internally displaced persons (IDPs) residing in informal shelters in Gaza City. This will be achieved by delivering15m3 of water per day through water trucking. Concurrently, Oxfam and its partner will undertake the repair of the water pipeline network at Al Jalaa Street, enhancing the discharge of Mekorot water to benefit 30,900 individuals, including both IDPs and host communities in Gaza City.

participating-org.narrative:
Oxfam Novib has been active in the Occupied Palestinian Territory/Israel (OPT/I) since 1982 and working with Palestinian refugees in Lebanon since the mid 1980s. It has built up a strong network of relationships with local NGOs and counts among its localcounterparts some of the largest and most professional NGOs in various sectors. It has accompanied these NGOs in their development from ad hoc volunteer groups to sizeable professional institutions with national outreach. At the same time the conceptualisation of the programme has evolved from three country programs in the early 1990s to a program for Palestinians in the Middle East (PME) working withPalestinians in OPT, Israel and Lebanon.
The programme has changed over the years with the establishment of the Palestinian Authority (PA) in the mid-1990s from a focus on support and service provision at a grassroots level and grassroots mobilization, to working towards influencing the establishment of the PA, its lawmaking and supporting building a democratic state # this involved supporting efforts of Palestinian civil society to build the basis for a democratic Palestinian state with room for civil participation, ensuring inclusion of vulnerable groups, refugees and women, and shaping its laws and systems. Oxfam Novib has also supported partners that are working on the provision of humanitarian assistance, response preparedness and conflict transformation. We have also supported partners in the provision of health services, access to quality education and gender justice.
